title: Claude skills: what they are and how to add one
h1: claude skills for people who do not write code
description: Learn what Claude skills contain, where to add a custom skill, and how to tell a reusable method apart from an app connection or a schedule.
answer: **stop explaining your review method every time you open a chat.** a claude skill keeps the instructions, scripts and reference material in a folder that loads when needed. it gives claude a repeatable way to work. as of 12 november 2026, anthropic lists skills across all plans, including free, with code execution enabled.[^1]

review.by: lead agent: independent reviewer pass against seo/facts (4 reviewers), every finding applied, automated gate

og_line: a reusable method, with its materials.

sections.h: put a usable method in the folder
sections.md:
**save the correction you are tired of making.** a skill gives claude a repeatable method for a particular task, using instructions, scripts and resources in a folder.[^1]

for a document review, that might mean:

- your writing rules
- an approved reference document
- a list of things the finished document must contain

write steps you could follow yourself. "compare dates in the draft with the brief" gives it a job. "make it excellent" leaves it guessing.

**your method goes in a zip; you do not need to build an app.** on individual plans, the setup as of 12 november 2026 is:[^2]

1. open settings, then capabilities
2. enable code execution and file creation
3. open customize, then skills
4. upload a zip of the skill folder

read its instructions and any scripts before enabling it, especially if someone else made the zip. start with a folder you understand.

sections.h: work out which piece is missing
sections.md:
**choose the piece that saves you repeating yourself.**

- **skill:** how to do the work, with its format and reference material
- **connector:** the app data or actions the job needs
- **schedule:** when to repeat it

anthropic’s connectors retrieve data and take actions in apps.[^3] [claude connectors](/guides/claude-connectors) covers access; [mcp](/guides/what-is-mcp) explains the connection standard. the skill teaches the method; the connector gets it to the material.

sections.h: make the first trial catch an error
sections.md:
**give it a document with a mistake you already know about.** a conflicting date, blank field or missing section makes a useful trial. ask for reasons beside each suggested change.

compare the answer with the document. did it flag the gap or fill it with a guess? that tells you more than asking the ai to grade itself.

use a short document without private material while you learn its habits. keep the method only if it catches the correction you built it for.

sections.h: do not build a skill for a one-off problem
sections.md:
**for a one-off request, just write the prompt.** if the audience and purpose change every time, fresh instructions may take less work than maintaining a skill.

build the folder when the same rules and references keep coming back. it will not fix a vague brief or reach an unavailable account. keep the smaller approach when it works.

want a desktop helper instead? start with the [non-developer guide](/guides/claude-code-for-non-developers). reusable instructions earn their keep when the work repeats.

faq.q: do i need a paid plan for skills?
faq.a: **no, free is on anthropic’s list.** as of 12 november 2026, it lists free, pro, max, ultra, team and enterprise. enable code execution first.[^1]

faq.q: are skills and connectors the same?
faq.a: **no, one teaches a method; the other provides access.** skills carry instructions and resources. connectors reach supported apps and actions.[^1][^3]

faq.q: can i upload a skill without writing scripts?
faq.a: **yes, a script is not required.** skills can contain instructions and resources too. upload a zip of the skill folder, using contents you understand.[^1][^2]

steps: write three corrections you repeat on the same kind of document
compare them with a skill folder you already have
read that folder’s instructions and any scripts
try its checklist on a short document you know well

rows: the same review method every time
files or actions in another app
the job should repeat at a set time
one unusual request with enough context

mistakes.mistake: uploading a zip without reading it
mistakes.fix: inspect the instructions and scripts before enabling the skill.
try a blank field or conflicting date and see whether the skill flags it.

tip.text: keep a skill only if you can name the repeated correction it saves you.
